correctness.rationale: The residue-group enumeration of two regular side-normal grids is valid for all 3≤n<m, including shared-normal endpoints. Formula (1) follows from splitting exactly n fine-grid gaps. The energy is strictly convex and reflection symmetric in phase, producing complete equality classes. Tangential polygon area equals r²Σ tan(g/2), and independent Simpson and polygon-clipping diagnostics support the exact formulas. The Haar mean is obtained by elementary telescoping integrals, and density/small-gap asymptotic from differentiation and a finite cubic-sum identity. The standalone verification program completed 5780 tests. No finite numerical experiment is invoked for the infinite-parameter claims.

value.rationale: For the canonical and geometrically natural problem of superimposing two unequal-resolution regular outer approximations of the same disk, exact overlap versus orientation is a nontrivial missing invariant. The theorem yields simultaneous optimal rotations for every convex function of the combined side-normal gaps, not just a one-off numeric calculation; sharp equality and facet transition counts; a complete random-area distribution and elementary mean; and a gcd²-controlled amplitude with a cubic decay law. These structural features offer reusable benchmarks for polygon discretization and stereological orientation models. The result is not a renaming of a basic tangential area identity, since that does not compute two-grid phase residues.
